chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from his uncle Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, richness and splendour wander around. When they acquire a place of reliance (on God), they settle.
A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Hassan — similar to it.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual condition that causes wealth and honor to settle permanently?
ai.summary: In the context of al-Kafi’s chapter on Tawakkul, this narration by Imam al-Sadiq (as) illustrates that material wealth and honor are inherently unstable ('joolan') until they find their spiritual anchor in a heart fully reliant on God. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that divine reliance transforms transient worldly status into enduring spiritual stability, preventing arrogance or anxiety.
